Revenue growth and Op Margin/Income (NTM) are forward analyst consensus from FMP (a single provider series whose basis is not designated as GAAP or non-GAAP); equity value & cash are point-in-time. Customer & net-retention metrics, where a company discloses them, are shown as cited callouts on the Target Profile (Exhibit C) — not here, as they are reported on non-comparable definitions. EPS Impact if Acquired reuses the deck's accretion engine (same premium / cash-stock mix / financing as the live deal; pre-synergy) modeling this acquirer buying each company — a real computation, not a fetch. ᵇ EV/EBITDA is n/mᵇ where D&A is not reported under a combined concept, so LTM EBITDA cannot be computed on a basis comparable to peers — an operating-income proxy is not shown, and components are not summed (a combined tag is not the sum of its parts). APPENDIX I
Sources & Methodology
Data provenance and basis of presentation · Buyer: Salesforce, Inc. · Target: Atlassian Corp
PRICING & MARKET DATA
·
Live share prices and 52-week trading ranges for the Buyer and the Target are sourced from CNBC and Nasdaq (keyless, near-real-time), captured as of August 9, 2026 and cross-checked across feeds where two agree.
·
Equity value (market capitalization) shown as "current" reflects the live price multiplied by reported shares outstanding; where a live price is unavailable it is shown as "—" or "N/A".
·
Intraday quotes and 52-week extremes depend on feed availability; where no source returns a range, an illustrative range built from monthly closes is labeled as such.
COMPANY FUNDAMENTALS — PRIMARY FILINGS
·
Company fundamentals — revenue, gross profit, net income, shares outstanding, cash, total debt, and free cash flow — are drawn from SEC EDGAR and Financial Modeling Prep: SEC EDGAR XBRL company facts (data.sec.gov) for domestic filers, with a period-matched Financial Modeling Prep value where a filer is a foreign private issuer or discontinues a concept. All are period-matched to each company’s fiscal year. EPS is the reported diluted EPS; net income ÷ weighted-average diluted shares is a labeled fallback only where a filer does not report diluted EPS.
·
Figures reflect each company’s most recent annual report (Form 10-K for domestic filers, Form 20-F for foreign private issuers) and are used as-is, without restatement adjustments.
·
Where a filer discontinues or freezes an XBRL concept (e.g. a gross-profit or long-term-debt tag), a period-matched Financial Modeling Prep value is substituted as a labeled fallback rather than carrying a stale figure.
ANALYST ESTIMATES & PRICE TARGETS
·
Forward revenue and EPS consensus — the FY-ahead estimate columns and the pro forma projections — are from Financial Modeling Prep analyst estimates: single-source, point-in-time, not guidance.
·
Per-firm price targets are from Financial Modeling Prep (price-target news and grades): the latest target per broker is kept, targets whose most recent call is over 18 months old are dropped, and statistical outliers (over 3× or under one-third of the panel median) are removed. Buy / hold / sell reflects the latest grade per firm.
·
An independent consensus cross-check (mean / high / low) draws on Nasdaq and Financial Modeling Prep where available. Price targets are sell-side FORECASTS, not guarantees.
VALUATION METHODOLOGIES
·
The analyst price-target range and the 52-week trading range supply market reference points. Precedent-transaction multiples are omitted deck-wide — no sourceable comparable public-deal set is available on the current data stack.
COMPANY & DESCRIPTIVE DATA
·
Company descriptions, CEO, headquarters, employee counts, IPO date, sector / industry classification, beta, average trading volume, and company logos are from the Financial Modeling Prep company profile.
·
Segment, geography, and customer-mix figures, where shown, are illustrative and are not company-disclosed breakdowns.
·
The pro-forma forward columns use sell-side ANALYST CONSENSUS estimates (via Financial Modeling Prep) for forward revenue and EPS — these are analyst forecasts, not the app’s own model. The accretion, synergy and combination MATH applied on top of those inputs IS the app’s model. Multi-year synergy ramps are model assumptions, not guidance; forward operating expense is shown as "—" rather than estimated.
BASIS OF PRESENTATION
·
All monetary figures are presented in US dollars, in millions ($M), as filed. $B is used only on market-cap, enterprise-value and deal-value summary lines.
·
Period basis: the screening comparables (Public Company Screen) and the company-profile financial snapshot are computed on a last-twelve-months (LTM) basis — latest annual plus the most recent interim year-to-date, less the prior-year interim — the standard banker screening convention; the pro-forma and accretion model is built on latest-fiscal-year actuals plus forward analyst consensus (a normalized forward basis). This split is deliberate, not an inconsistency. Foreign private issuers without SEC interim (10-Q) filings, and any filer whose interim data does not tie out, are shown on a fiscal-year basis and labeled "FY".
·
Calendarization: where the two companies have different fiscal year-ends, the LTM screening basis is used specifically because it aligns their measurement windows to within approximately one month — materially reducing the fiscal-year-end offset that a same-labeled "FY" comparison would carry. Full calendar-year restatement is deliberately NOT applied: it would require estimating unfiled interim quarters (interpolation of periods no filer reports), and the residual period difference on the LTM basis is immaterial (under ~2% of the affected figures). The pro-forma / accretion model, being built on latest-fiscal-year actuals + forward consensus, pairs each company’s own latest fiscal year (relative years, not a common calendar period) — stated on that slide.
·
Enterprise value (EV) = equity value (market capitalization) + total debt − cash & marketable securities, taken from the same filing; figures for companies with active share-repurchase programs are approximate.
·
Profitability on the standalone P&L and comparative-profile slides — operating income, net income, diluted EPS, and operating/net margins — is shown on a Non-GAAP basis as reported in each company’s fiscal year-end earnings release (Form 8-K, Item 2.02), period-matched to the fiscal year shown and reconciled to GAAP; each line is labeled, and falls back to a GAAP-labeled figure where a reconciled non-GAAP value was unavailable. Gross profit, gross margin and operating expenses remain GAAP; EBITDA and its margins are computed (operating income + D&A); revenue and share counts are basis-neutral.
·
The accretion, pro forma and relative-contribution views are built on each company’s reported GAAP figures and are labeled accordingly.
·
Fiscal years follow each company’s own filing calendar: the Buyer FY2026, the Target FY2025.
·
Numbers are rounded for presentation; minor differences may arise from rounding.
TRANSACTION ASSUMPTIONS
·
Offer price, acquisition premium, and cash/stock consideration mix are user- or model-defined inputs.
·
Year 1–Year 3 synergies and transaction fees are user/model assumptions, not negotiated terms.
·
A 21% marginal tax rate and a 5% interest rate on acquisition debt are applied as standing model assumptions.
DISCLAIMER
·
This document is an educational illustration generated by EasyM&A to model a hypothetical combination of the Buyer and the Target.
·
It is NOT investment, financial, legal, or tax advice, NOT a recommendation or solicitation, and NOT an offer to buy or sell any security. It does not constitute a fairness opinion and MUST NOT be relied upon for any investment, purchase, sale, or other financial decision.
·
All outputs are hypothetical and must be independently verified against primary sources (SEC filings and live market data) before any decision. Market data as of August 9, 2026; subject to change.

PRICING & MARKET DATA
·
Live share prices and 52-week trading ranges for the Buyer and the Target are sourced from CNBC and Nasdaq (keyless, near-real-time), captured as of August 9, 2026 and cross-checked across feeds where two agree.

COMPANY FUNDAMENTALS — PRIMARY FILINGS
·
Company fundamentals — revenue, gross profit, net income, shares outstanding, cash, total debt, and free cash flow — are drawn from SEC EDGAR and Financial Modeling Prep: SEC EDGAR XBRL company facts (data.sec.gov) for domestic filers, with a period-matched Financial Modeling Prep value where a filer is a foreign private issuer or discontinues a concept. All are period-matched to each company’s fiscal year. EPS is the reported diluted EPS; net income ÷ weighted-average diluted shares is a labeled fallback only where a filer does not report diluted EPS.
·
Figures reflect each company’s most recent annual report (Form 10-K for domestic filers, Form 20-F for foreign private issuers) and are used as-is, without restatement adjustments.
·
Where a filer discontinues or freezes an XBRL concept (e.g. a gross-profit or long-term-debt tag), a period-matched Financial Modeling Prep value is substituted as a labeled fallback rather than carrying a stale figure.
ANALYST ESTIMATES & PRICE TARGETS
·
Forward revenue and EPS consensus — the FY-ahead estimate columns and the pro forma projections — are from Financial Modeling Prep analyst estimates: single-source, point-in-time, not guidance.

Per-firm price targets are from Financial Modeling Prep (price-target news and grades): the latest target per broker is kept, targets whose most recent call is over 18 months old are dropped, and statistical outliers (over 3× or under one-third of the panel median) are removed. Buy / hold / sell reflects the latest grade per firm.
·
An independent consensus cross-check (mean / high / low) draws on Nasdaq and Financial Modeling Prep where available. Price targets are sell-side FORECASTS, not guarantees.
VALUATION METHODOLOGIES
·
The analyst price-target range and the 52-week trading range supply market reference points. Precedent-transaction multiples are omitted deck-wide — no sourceable comparable public-deal set is available on the current data stack.
COMPANY & DESCRIPTIVE DATA
·
Company descriptions, CEO, headquarters, employee counts, IPO date, sector / industry classification, beta, average trading volume, and company logos are from the Financial Modeling Prep company profile.
·
Segment, geography, and customer-mix figures, where shown, are illustrative and are not company-disclosed breakdowns.
·
The pro-forma forward columns use sell-side ANALYST CONSENSUS estimates (via Financial Modeling Prep) for forward revenue and EPS — these are analyst forecasts, not the app’s own model. The accretion, synergy and combination MATH applied on top of those inputs IS the app’s model. Multi-year synergy ramps are model assumptions, not guidance; forward operating expense is shown as "—" rather than estimated.
BASIS OF PRESENTATION
·
All monetary figures are presented in US dollars, in millions ($M), as filed. $B is used only on market-cap, enterprise-value and deal-value summary lines.
·
Period basis: the screening comparables (Public Company Screen) and the company-profile financial snapshot are computed on a last-twelve-months (LTM) basis — latest annual plus the most recent interim year-to-date, less the prior-year interim — the standard banker screening convention; the pro-forma and accretion model is built on latest-fiscal-year actuals plus forward analyst consensus (a normalized forward basis). This split is deliberate, not an inconsistency. Foreign private issuers without SEC interim (10-Q) filings, and any filer whose interim data does not tie out, are shown on a fiscal-year basis and labeled "FY".
·
Calendarization: where the two companies have different fiscal year-ends, the LTM screening basis is used specifically because it aligns their measurement windows to within approximately one month — materially reducing the fiscal-year-end offset that a same-labeled "FY" comparison would carry. Full calendar-year restatement is deliberately NOT applied: it would require estimating unfiled interim quarters (interpolation of periods no filer reports), and the residual period difference on the LTM basis is immaterial (under ~2% of the affected figures). The pro-forma / accretion model, being built on latest-fiscal-year actuals + forward consensus, pairs each company’s own latest fiscal year (relative years, not a common calendar period) — stated on that slide.
·
Enterprise value (EV) = equity value (market capitalization) + total debt − cash & marketable securities, taken from the same filing; figures for companies with active share-repurchase programs are approximate.
·
Profitability on the standalone P&L and comparative-profile slides — operating income, net income, diluted EPS, and operating/net margins — is shown on a Non-GAAP basis as reported in each company’s fiscal year-end earnings release (Form 8-K, Item 2.02), period-matched to the fiscal year shown and reconciled to GAAP; each line is labeled, and falls back to a GAAP-labeled figure where a reconciled non-GAAP value was unavailable. Gross profit, gross margin and operating expenses remain GAAP; EBITDA and its margins are computed (operating income + D&A); revenue and share counts are basis-neutral.
·
The accretion, pro forma and relative-contribution views are built on each company’s reported GAAP figures and are labeled accordingly.
·
Fiscal years follow each company’s own filing calendar: the Buyer FY2026, the Target FY2025.
·
Numbers are rounded for presentation; minor differences may arise from rounding.

·
Year 1–Year 3 synergies and transaction fees are user/model assumptions, not negotiated terms.

APPENDIX I
Sources & Methodology
Data provenance and basis of presentation · Buyer: Jpmorgan Chase & Co · Target: Bank of America Corp
PRICING & MARKET DATA
·
Live share prices and 52-week trading ranges for the Buyer and the Target are sourced from CNBC and Nasdaq (keyless, near-real-time), captured as of August 9, 2026 and cross-checked across feeds where two agree.
·
Equity value (market capitalization) shown as "current" reflects the live price multiplied by reported shares outstanding; where a live price is unavailable it is shown as "—" or "N/A".
·
Intraday quotes and 52-week extremes depend on feed availability; where no source returns a range, an illustrative range built from monthly closes is labeled as such.
COMPANY FUNDAMENTALS — PRIMARY FILINGS
·
Company fundamentals — revenue, gross profit, net income, shares outstanding, cash, total debt, and free cash flow — are drawn from SEC EDGAR and Financial Modeling Prep: SEC EDGAR XBRL company facts (data.sec.gov) for domestic filers, with a period-matched Financial Modeling Prep value where a filer is a foreign private issuer or discontinues a concept. All are period-matched to each company’s fiscal year. EPS is the reported diluted EPS; net income ÷ weighted-average diluted shares is a labeled fallback only where a filer does not report diluted EPS.
·
Figures reflect each company’s most recent annual report (Form 10-K for domestic filers, Form 20-F for foreign private issuers) and are used as-is, without restatement adjustments.
·
Where a filer discontinues or freezes an XBRL concept (e.g. a gross-profit or long-term-debt tag), a period-matched Financial Modeling Prep value is substituted as a labeled fallback rather than carrying a stale figure.
ANALYST ESTIMATES & PRICE TARGETS
·
Forward revenue and EPS consensus — the FY-ahead estimate columns and the pro forma projections — are from Financial Modeling Prep analyst estimates: single-source, point-in-time, not guidance.
·
Per-firm price targets are from Financial Modeling Prep (price-target news and grades): the latest target per broker is kept, targets whose most recent call is over 18 months old are dropped, and statistical outliers (over 3× or under one-third of the panel median) are removed. Buy / hold / sell reflects the latest grade per firm.
·
An independent consensus cross-check (mean / high / low) draws on Nasdaq and Financial Modeling Prep where available. Price targets are sell-side FORECASTS, not guarantees.
VALUATION METHODOLOGIES
·
The analyst price-target range and the 52-week trading range supply market reference points. Precedent-transaction multiples are omitted deck-wide — no sourceable comparable public-deal set is available on the current data stack.
COMPANY & DESCRIPTIVE DATA
·
Company descriptions, CEO, headquarters, employee counts, IPO date, sector / industry classification, beta, average trading volume, and company logos are from the Financial Modeling Prep company profile.
·
Segment, geography, and customer-mix figures, where shown, are illustrative and are not company-disclosed breakdowns.
·
The pro-forma forward columns use sell-side ANALYST CONSENSUS estimates (via Financial Modeling Prep) for forward revenue and EPS — these are analyst forecasts, not the app’s own model. The accretion, synergy and combination MATH applied on top of those inputs IS the app’s model. Multi-year synergy ramps are model assumptions, not guidance; forward operating expense is shown as "—" rather than estimated.
BASIS OF PRESENTATION
·
All monetary figures are presented in US dollars, in millions ($M), as filed. $B is used only on market-cap, enterprise-value and deal-value summary lines.
·
Period basis: the screening comparables (Public Company Screen) and the company-profile financial snapshot are computed on a last-twelve-months (LTM) basis — latest annual plus the most recent interim year-to-date, less the prior-year interim — the standard banker screening convention; the pro-forma and accretion model is built on latest-fiscal-year actuals plus forward analyst consensus (a normalized forward basis). This split is deliberate, not an inconsistency. Foreign private issuers without SEC interim (10-Q) filings, and any filer whose interim data does not tie out, are shown on a fiscal-year basis and labeled "FY".
·
Calendarization: where the two companies have different fiscal year-ends, the LTM screening basis is used specifically because it aligns their measurement windows to within approximately one month — materially reducing the fiscal-year-end offset that a same-labeled "FY" comparison would carry. Full calendar-year restatement is deliberately NOT applied: it would require estimating unfiled interim quarters (interpolation of periods no filer reports), and the residual period difference on the LTM basis is immaterial (under ~2% of the affected figures). The pro-forma / accretion model, being built on latest-fiscal-year actuals + forward consensus, pairs each company’s own latest fiscal year (relative years, not a common calendar period) — stated on that slide.
·
Enterprise value (EV) = equity value (market capitalization) + total debt − cash & marketable securities, taken from the same filing; figures for companies with active share-repurchase programs are approximate.
·
Profitability on the standalone P&L and comparative-profile slides — operating income, net income, diluted EPS, and operating/net margins — is shown on a Non-GAAP basis as reported in each company’s fiscal year-end earnings release (Form 8-K, Item 2.02), period-matched to the fiscal year shown and reconciled to GAAP; each line is labeled, and falls back to a GAAP-labeled figure where a reconciled non-GAAP value was unavailable. Gross profit, gross margin and operating expenses remain GAAP; EBITDA and its margins are computed (operating income + D&A); revenue and share counts are basis-neutral.
·
The accretion, pro forma and relative-contribution views are built on each company’s reported GAAP figures and are labeled accordingly.
·
Fiscal years follow each company’s own filing calendar: the Buyer FY2025, the Target FY2025.
·
Numbers are rounded for presentation; minor differences may arise from rounding.
TRANSACTION ASSUMPTIONS
·
Offer price, acquisition premium, and cash/stock consideration mix are user- or model-defined inputs.
·
Year 1–Year 3 synergies and transaction fees are user/model assumptions, not negotiated terms.
·
A 21% marginal tax rate and a 5% interest rate on acquisition debt are applied as standing model assumptions.

Sources & Methodology

PRICING & MARKET DATA
·
Live share prices and 52-week trading ranges for the Buyer and the Target are sourced from CNBC and Nasdaq (keyless, near-real-time), captured as of August 9, 2026 and cross-checked across feeds where two agree.

·
Intraday quotes and 52-week extremes depend on feed availability; where no source returns a range, an illustrative range built from monthly closes is labeled as such.
COMPANY FUNDAMENTALS — PRIMARY FILINGS
·
Company fundamentals — revenue, gross profit, net income, shares outstanding, cash, total debt, and free cash flow — are drawn from SEC EDGAR and Financial Modeling Prep: SEC EDGAR XBRL company facts (data.sec.gov) for domestic filers, with a period-matched Financial Modeling Prep value where a filer is a foreign private issuer or discontinues a concept. All are period-matched to each company’s fiscal year. EPS is the reported diluted EPS; net income ÷ weighted-average diluted shares is a labeled fallback only where a filer does not report diluted EPS.
·
Figures reflect each company’s most recent annual report (Form 10-K for domestic filers, Form 20-F for foreign private issuers) and are used as-is, without restatement adjustments.
·
Where a filer discontinues or freezes an XBRL concept (e.g. a gross-profit or long-term-debt tag), a period-matched Financial Modeling Prep value is substituted as a labeled fallback rather than carrying a stale figure.
ANALYST ESTIMATES & PRICE TARGETS
·
Forward revenue and EPS consensus — the FY-ahead estimate columns and the pro forma projections — are from Financial Modeling Prep analyst estimates: single-source, point-in-time, not guidance.
·
Per-firm price targets are from Financial Modeling Prep (price-target news and grades): the latest target per broker is kept, targets whose most recent call is over 18 months old are dropped, and statistical outliers (over 3× or under one-third of the panel median) are removed. Buy / hold / sell reflects the latest grade per firm.
·
An independent consensus cross-check (mean / high / low) draws on Nasdaq and Financial Modeling Prep where available. Price targets are sell-side FORECASTS, not guarantees.
VALUATION METHODOLOGIES
·
The analyst price-target range and the 52-week trading range supply market reference points. Precedent-transaction multiples are omitted deck-wide — no sourceable comparable public-deal set is available on the current data stack.
COMPANY & DESCRIPTIVE DATA
·
Company descriptions, CEO, headquarters, employee counts, IPO date, sector / industry classification, beta, average trading volume, and company logos are from the Financial Modeling Prep company profile.
·
Segment, geography, and customer-mix figures, where shown, are illustrative and are not company-disclosed breakdowns.
·
The pro-forma forward columns use sell-side ANALYST CONSENSUS estimates (via Financial Modeling Prep) for forward revenue and EPS — these are analyst forecasts, not the app’s own model. The accretion, synergy and combination MATH applied on top of those inputs IS the app’s model. Multi-year synergy ramps are model assumptions, not guidance; forward operating expense is shown as "—" rather than estimated.
BASIS OF PRESENTATION
·
All monetary figures are presented in US dollars, in millions ($M), as filed. $B is used only on market-cap, enterprise-value and deal-value summary lines.
·
Period basis: the screening comparables (Public Company Screen) and the company-profile financial snapshot are computed on a last-twelve-months (LTM) basis — latest annual plus the most recent interim year-to-date, less the prior-year interim — the standard banker screening convention; the pro-forma and accretion model is built on latest-fiscal-year actuals plus forward analyst consensus (a normalized forward basis). This split is deliberate, not an inconsistency. Foreign private issuers without SEC interim (10-Q) filings, and any filer whose interim data does not tie out, are shown on a fiscal-year basis and labeled "FY".
·
Calendarization: where the two companies have different fiscal year-ends, the LTM screening basis is used specifically because it aligns their measurement windows to within approximately one month — materially reducing the fiscal-year-end offset that a same-labeled "FY" comparison would carry. Full calendar-year restatement is deliberately NOT applied: it would require estimating unfiled interim quarters (interpolation of periods no filer reports), and the residual period difference on the LTM basis is immaterial (under ~2% of the affected figures). The pro-forma / accretion model, being built on latest-fiscal-year actuals + forward consensus, pairs each company’s own latest fiscal year (relative years, not a common calendar period) — stated on that slide.
·

APPENDIX I
Sources & Methodology
Data provenance and basis of presentation · Buyer: Mcdonalds Corp · Target: Red Robin Gourmet Burgers Inc
PRICING & MARKET DATA
·
Live share prices and 52-week trading ranges for the Buyer and the Target are sourced from CNBC and Nasdaq (keyless, near-real-time), captured as of August 9, 2026 and cross-checked across feeds where two agree.
·
Equity value (market capitalization) shown as "current" reflects the live price multiplied by reported shares outstanding; where a live price is unavailable it is shown as "—" or "N/A".
·
Intraday quotes and 52-week extremes depend on feed availability; where no source returns a range, an illustrative range built from monthly closes is labeled as such.
COMPANY FUNDAMENTALS — PRIMARY FILINGS
·
Company fundamentals — revenue, gross profit, net income, shares outstanding, cash, total debt, and free cash flow — are drawn from SEC EDGAR and Financial Modeling Prep: SEC EDGAR XBRL company facts (data.sec.gov) for domestic filers, with a period-matched Financial Modeling Prep value where a filer is a foreign private issuer or discontinues a concept. All are period-matched to each company’s fiscal year. EPS is the reported diluted EPS; net income ÷ weighted-average diluted shares is a labeled fallback only where a filer does not report diluted EPS.
·
Figures reflect each company’s most recent annual report (Form 10-K for domestic filers, Form 20-F for foreign private issuers) and are used as-is, without restatement adjustments.
·
Where a filer discontinues or freezes an XBRL concept (e.g. a gross-profit or long-term-debt tag), a period-matched Financial Modeling Prep value is substituted as a labeled fallback rather than carrying a stale figure.
ANALYST ESTIMATES & PRICE TARGETS
·
Forward revenue and EPS consensus — the FY-ahead estimate columns and the pro forma projections — are from Financial Modeling Prep analyst estimates: single-source, point-in-time, not guidance.
·
Per-firm price targets are from Financial Modeling Prep (price-target news and grades): the latest target per broker is kept, targets whose most recent call is over 18 months old are dropped, and statistical outliers (over 3× or under one-third of the panel median) are removed. Buy / hold / sell reflects the latest grade per firm.
·
An independent consensus cross-check (mean / high / low) draws on Nasdaq and Financial Modeling Prep where available. Price targets are sell-side FORECASTS, not guarantees.
VALUATION METHODOLOGIES
·
The analyst price-target range and the 52-week trading range supply market reference points. Precedent-transaction multiples are omitted deck-wide — no sourceable comparable public-deal set is available on the current data stack.
COMPANY & DESCRIPTIVE DATA
·
Company descriptions, CEO, headquarters, employee counts, IPO date, sector / industry classification, beta, average trading volume, and company logos are from the Financial Modeling Prep company profile.
·
Segment, geography, and customer-mix figures, where shown, are illustrative and are not company-disclosed breakdowns.
·
The pro-forma forward columns use sell-side ANALYST CONSENSUS estimates (via Financial Modeling Prep) for forward revenue and EPS — these are analyst forecasts, not the app’s own model. The accretion, synergy and combination MATH applied on top of those inputs IS the app’s model. Multi-year synergy ramps are model assumptions, not guidance; forward operating expense is shown as "—" rather than estimated.
BASIS OF PRESENTATION
·
All monetary figures are presented in US dollars, in millions ($M), as filed. $B is used only on market-cap, enterprise-value and deal-value summary lines.
·
Period basis: the screening comparables (Public Company Screen) and the company-profile financial snapshot are computed on a last-twelve-months (LTM) basis — latest annual plus the most recent interim year-to-date, less the prior-year interim — the standard banker screening convention; the pro-forma and accretion model is built on latest-fiscal-year actuals plus forward analyst consensus (a normalized forward basis). This split is deliberate, not an inconsistency. Foreign private issuers without SEC interim (10-Q) filings, and any filer whose interim data does not tie out, are shown on a fiscal-year basis and labeled "FY".
·
Calendarization: where the two companies have different fiscal year-ends, the LTM screening basis is used specifically because it aligns their measurement windows to within approximately one month — materially reducing the fiscal-year-end offset that a same-labeled "FY" comparison would carry. Full calendar-year restatement is deliberately NOT applied: it would require estimating unfiled interim quarters (interpolation of periods no filer reports), and the residual period difference on the LTM basis is immaterial (under ~2% of the affected figures). The pro-forma / accretion model, being built on latest-fiscal-year actuals + forward consensus, pairs each company’s own latest fiscal year (relative years, not a common calendar period) — stated on that slide.
·
Enterprise value (EV) = equity value (market capitalization) + total debt − cash & marketable securities, taken from the same filing; figures for companies with active share-repurchase programs are approximate.
·
Profitability on the standalone P&L and comparative-profile slides — operating income, net income, diluted EPS, and operating/net margins — is shown on a Non-GAAP basis as reported in each company’s fiscal year-end earnings release (Form 8-K, Item 2.02), period-matched to the fiscal year shown and reconciled to GAAP; each line is labeled, and falls back to a GAAP-labeled figure where a reconciled non-GAAP value was unavailable. Gross profit, gross margin and operating expenses remain GAAP; EBITDA and its margins are computed (operating income + D&A); revenue and share counts are basis-neutral.
·
The accretion, pro forma and relative-contribution views are built on each company’s reported GAAP figures and are labeled accordingly.
·
Fiscal years follow each company’s own filing calendar: the Buyer FY2025, the Target FY2025.
·
Numbers are rounded for presentation; minor differences may arise from rounding.
TRANSACTION ASSUMPTIONS
·
Offer price, acquisition premium, and cash/stock consideration mix are user- or model-defined inputs.
·
Year 1–Year 3 synergies and transaction fees are user/model assumptions, not negotiated terms.
·
A 21% marginal tax rate and a 5% interest rate on acquisition debt are applied as standing model assumptions.
DISCLAIMER

·
It is NOT investment, financial, legal, or tax advice, NOT a recommendation or solicitation, and NOT an offer to buy or sell any security. It does not constitute a fairness opinion and MUST NOT be relied upon for any investment, purchase, sale, or other financial decision.

Company fundamentals — revenue, gross profit, net income, shares outstanding, cash, total debt, and free cash flow — are drawn from SEC EDGAR and Financial Modeling Prep: SEC EDGAR XBRL company facts (data.sec.gov) for domestic filers, with a period-matched Financial Modeling Prep value where a filer is a foreign private issuer or discontinues a concept. ·

APPENDIX I
Sources & Methodology
Data provenance and basis of presentation · Buyer: Coca Cola Co · Target: Nestlé S.A.
PRICING & MARKET DATA
·
Live share prices and 52-week trading ranges for the Buyer and the Target are sourced from CNBC and Nasdaq (keyless, near-real-time), captured as of August 9, 2026 and cross-checked across feeds where two agree.
·
Equity value (market capitalization) shown as "current" reflects the live price multiplied by reported shares outstanding; where a live price is unavailable it is shown as "—" or "N/A".
·
Intraday quotes and 52-week extremes depend on feed availability; where no source returns a range, an illustrative range built from monthly closes is labeled as such.
COMPANY FUNDAMENTALS — PRIMARY FILINGS
·
Company fundamentals — revenue, gross profit, net income, shares outstanding, cash, total debt, and free cash flow — are drawn from SEC EDGAR and Financial Modeling Prep: SEC EDGAR XBRL company facts (data.sec.gov) for domestic filers, with a period-matched Financial Modeling Prep value where a filer is a foreign private issuer or discontinues a concept. All are period-matched to each company’s fiscal year. EPS is the reported diluted EPS; net income ÷ weighted-average diluted shares is a labeled fallback only where a filer does not report diluted EPS.
·
Figures reflect each company’s most recent annual report (Form 10-K for domestic filers, Form 20-F for foreign private issuers) and are used as-is, without restatement adjustments.
·
Where a filer discontinues or freezes an XBRL concept (e.g. a gross-profit or long-term-debt tag), a period-matched Financial Modeling Prep value is substituted as a labeled fallback rather than carrying a stale figure.
ANALYST ESTIMATES & PRICE TARGETS
·
Forward revenue and EPS consensus — the FY-ahead estimate columns and the pro forma projections — are from Financial Modeling Prep analyst estimates: single-source, point-in-time, not guidance.
·
Per-firm price targets are from Financial Modeling Prep (price-target news and grades): the latest target per broker is kept, targets whose most recent call is over 18 months old are dropped, and statistical outliers (over 3× or under one-third of the panel median) are removed. Buy / hold / sell reflects the latest grade per firm.
·
An independent consensus cross-check (mean / high / low) draws on Nasdaq and Financial Modeling Prep where available. Price targets are sell-side FORECASTS, not guarantees.
VALUATION METHODOLOGIES
·
The analyst price-target range and the 52-week trading range supply market reference points. Precedent-transaction multiples are omitted deck-wide — no sourceable comparable public-deal set is available on the current data stack.
COMPANY & DESCRIPTIVE DATA
·
Company descriptions, CEO, headquarters, employee counts, IPO date, sector / industry classification, beta, average trading volume, and company logos are from the Financial Modeling Prep company profile.
·
Segment, geography, and customer-mix figures, where shown, are illustrative and are not company-disclosed breakdowns.
·
The pro-forma forward columns use sell-side ANALYST CONSENSUS estimates (via Financial Modeling Prep) for forward revenue and EPS — these are analyst forecasts, not the app’s own model. The accretion, synergy and combination MATH applied on top of those inputs IS the app’s model. Multi-year synergy ramps are model assumptions, not guidance; forward operating expense is shown as "—" rather than estimated.
BASIS OF PRESENTATION
·
All monetary figures are presented in US dollars, in millions ($M). Domestic filers report in USD and are shown as filed. Where a company reports in another currency — here Nestlé S.A., reported in CHF — figures are converted to USD: income-statement and cash-flow items at the fiscal-year average rate (FY2025 average CHF→USD 1.2061) and balance-sheet items at the spot rate on the data date (1.2373). Share counts, and any figure already in USD (e.g. an ADR market price), are not converted. $B is used only on market-cap, enterprise-value and deal-value summary lines.
·
Period basis: the screening comparables (Public Company Screen) and the company-profile financial snapshot are computed on a last-twelve-months (LTM) basis — latest annual plus the most recent interim year-to-date, less the prior-year interim — the standard banker screening convention; the pro-forma and accretion model is built on latest-fiscal-year actuals plus forward analyst consensus (a normalized forward basis). This split is deliberate, not an inconsistency. Foreign private issuers without SEC interim (10-Q) filings, and any filer whose interim data does not tie out, are shown on a fiscal-year basis and labeled "FY".
·
Calendarization: where the two companies have different fiscal year-ends, the LTM screening basis is used specifically because it aligns their measurement windows to within approximately one month — materially reducing the fiscal-year-end offset that a same-labeled "FY" comparison would carry. Full calendar-year restatement is deliberately NOT applied: it would require estimating unfiled interim quarters (interpolation of periods no filer reports), and the residual period difference on the LTM basis is immaterial (under ~2% of the affected figures). The pro-forma / accretion model, being built on latest-fiscal-year actuals + forward consensus, pairs each company’s own latest fiscal year (relative years, not a common calendar period) — stated on that slide.
·
Enterprise value (EV) = equity value (market capitalization) + total debt − cash & marketable securities, taken from the same filing; figures for companies with active share-repurchase programs are approximate.
·
Profitability on the standalone P&L and comparative-profile slides — operating income, net income, diluted EPS, and operating/net margins — is shown on a Non-GAAP basis as reported in each company’s fiscal year-end earnings release (Form 8-K, Item 2.02), period-matched to the fiscal year shown and reconciled to GAAP; each line is labeled, and falls back to a GAAP-labeled figure where a reconciled non-GAAP value was unavailable. Gross profit, gross margin and operating expenses remain GAAP; EBITDA and its margins are computed (operating income + D&A); revenue and share counts are basis-neutral.
·
The accretion, pro forma and relative-contribution views are built on each company’s reported GAAP figures and are labeled accordingly.
·
Fiscal years follow each company’s own filing calendar: the Buyer FY2025, the Target FY—.
·
Numbers are rounded for presentation; minor differences may arise from rounding.
TRANSACTION ASSUMPTIONS
·
Offer price, acquisition premium, and cash/stock consideration mix are user- or model-defined inputs.
·
Year 1–Year 3 synergies and transaction fees are user/model assumptions, not negotiated terms.
·
A 21% marginal tax rate and a 5% interest rate on acquisition debt are applied as standing model assumptions.
DISCLAIMER
·
This document is an educational illustration generated by EasyM&A to model a hypothetical combination of the Buyer and the Target.
·
It is NOT investment, financial, legal, or tax advice, NOT a recommendation or solicitation, and NOT an offer to buy or sell any security. It does not constitute a fairness opinion and MUST NOT be relied upon for any investment, purchase, sale, or other financial decision.
·
All outputs are hypothetical and must be independently verified against primary sources (SEC filings and live market data) before any decision. Market data as of August 9, 2026; subject to change.
Sources: SEC EDGAR and Financial Modeling Prep for company fundamentals; CNBC and Nasdaq for live pricing; Nasdaq and Financial Modeling Prep for the consensus price-target cross-check; Financial Modeling Prep for per-firm price targets, forward analyst estimates, and company profiles. Estimated and assumption-based figures are labeled throughout. Educational use only — not investment advice.

BASIS OF PRESENTATION
·
All monetary figures are presented in US dollars, in millions ($M). Domestic filers report in USD and are shown as filed. Where a company reports in another currency — here Nestlé S.A., reported in CHF — figures are converted to USD: income-statement and cash-flow items at the fiscal-year average rate (FY2025 average CHF→USD 1.2061) and balance-sheet items at the spot rate on the data date (1.2373). The pro-forma / accretion model, being built on latest-fiscal-year actuals + forward consensus, pairs each company’s own latest fiscal year (relative years, not a common calendar period) — stated on that slide.

APPENDIX I
Sources & Methodology
Data provenance and basis of presentation · Buyer: Rocket Lab Corp · Target: Iridium Communications Inc.
PRICING & MARKET DATA
·
Live share prices and 52-week trading ranges for the Buyer and the Target are sourced from CNBC and Nasdaq (keyless, near-real-time), captured as of August 9, 2026 and cross-checked across feeds where two agree.
·
Equity value (market capitalization) shown as "current" reflects the live price multiplied by reported shares outstanding; where a live price is unavailable it is shown as "—" or "N/A".
·
Intraday quotes and 52-week extremes depend on feed availability; where no source returns a range, an illustrative range built from monthly closes is labeled as such.
COMPANY FUNDAMENTALS — PRIMARY FILINGS
·
Company fundamentals — revenue, gross profit, net income, shares outstanding, cash, total debt, and free cash flow — are drawn from SEC EDGAR and Financial Modeling Prep: SEC EDGAR XBRL company facts (data.sec.gov) for domestic filers, with a period-matched Financial Modeling Prep value where a filer is a foreign private issuer or discontinues a concept. All are period-matched to each company’s fiscal year. EPS is the reported diluted EPS; net income ÷ weighted-average diluted shares is a labeled fallback only where a filer does not report diluted EPS.
·
Figures reflect each company’s most recent annual report (Form 10-K for domestic filers, Form 20-F for foreign private issuers) and are used as-is, without restatement adjustments.
·
Where a filer discontinues or freezes an XBRL concept (e.g. a gross-profit or long-term-debt tag), a period-matched Financial Modeling Prep value is substituted as a labeled fallback rather than carrying a stale figure.
ANALYST ESTIMATES & PRICE TARGETS
·
Forward revenue and EPS consensus — the FY-ahead estimate columns and the pro forma projections — are from Financial Modeling Prep analyst estimates: single-source, point-in-time, not guidance.
·
Per-firm price targets are from Financial Modeling Prep (price-target news and grades): the latest target per broker is kept, targets whose most recent call is over 18 months old are dropped, and statistical outliers (over 3× or under one-third of the panel median) are removed. Buy / hold / sell reflects the latest grade per firm.
·
An independent consensus cross-check (mean / high / low) draws on Nasdaq and Financial Modeling Prep where available. Price targets are sell-side FORECASTS, not guarantees.
VALUATION METHODOLOGIES
·
The analyst price-target range and the 52-week trading range supply market reference points. Precedent-transaction multiples are omitted deck-wide — no sourceable comparable public-deal set is available on the current data stack.
COMPANY & DESCRIPTIVE DATA
·
Company descriptions, CEO, headquarters, employee counts, IPO date, sector / industry classification, beta, average trading volume, and company logos are from the Financial Modeling Prep company profile.
·
Segment, geography, and customer-mix figures, where shown, are illustrative and are not company-disclosed breakdowns.
·
The pro-forma forward columns use sell-side ANALYST CONSENSUS estimates (via Financial Modeling Prep) for forward revenue and EPS — these are analyst forecasts, not the app’s own model. The accretion, synergy and combination MATH applied on top of those inputs IS the app’s model. Multi-year synergy ramps are model assumptions, not guidance; forward operating expense is shown as "—" rather than estimated.
BASIS OF PRESENTATION
·
All monetary figures are presented in US dollars, in millions ($M), as filed. $B is used only on market-cap, enterprise-value and deal-value summary lines.
·
Period basis: the screening comparables (Public Company Screen) and the company-profile financial snapshot are computed on a last-twelve-months (LTM) basis — latest annual plus the most recent interim year-to-date, less the prior-year interim — the standard banker screening convention; the pro-forma and accretion model is built on latest-fiscal-year actuals plus forward analyst consensus (a normalized forward basis). This split is deliberate, not an inconsistency. Foreign private issuers without SEC interim (10-Q) filings, and any filer whose interim data does not tie out, are shown on a fiscal-year basis and labeled "FY".
·
Calendarization: where the two companies have different fiscal year-ends, the LTM screening basis is used specifically because it aligns their measurement windows to within approximately one month — materially reducing the fiscal-year-end offset that a same-labeled "FY" comparison would carry. Full calendar-year restatement is deliberately NOT applied: it would require estimating unfiled interim quarters (interpolation of periods no filer reports), and the residual period difference on the LTM basis is immaterial (under ~2% of the affected figures). The pro-forma / accretion model, being built on latest-fiscal-year actuals + forward consensus, pairs each company’s own latest fiscal year (relative years, not a common calendar period) — stated on that slide.
·
Enterprise value (EV) = equity value (market capitalization) + total debt − cash & marketable securities, taken from the same filing; figures for companies with active share-repurchase programs are approximate.
·
Profitability on the standalone P&L and comparative-profile slides — operating income, net income, diluted EPS, and operating/net margins — is shown on a Non-GAAP basis as reported in each company’s fiscal year-end earnings release (Form 8-K, Item 2.02), period-matched to the fiscal year shown and reconciled to GAAP; each line is labeled, and falls back to a GAAP-labeled figure where a reconciled non-GAAP value was unavailable. Gross profit, gross margin and operating expenses remain GAAP; EBITDA and its margins are computed (operating income + D&A); revenue and share counts are basis-neutral.
·
The accretion, pro forma and relative-contribution views are built on each company’s reported GAAP figures and are labeled accordingly.
·
Fiscal years follow each company’s own filing calendar: the Buyer FY2025, the Target FY2025.
·
Numbers are rounded for presentation; minor differences may arise from rounding.
TRANSACTION ASSUMPTIONS
·
Offer price, acquisition premium, and cash/stock consideration mix are user- or model-defined inputs.
·
Year 1–Year 3 synergies and transaction fees are user/model assumptions, not negotiated terms.
·
A 21% marginal tax rate and a 5% interest rate on acquisition debt are applied as standing model assumptions.
DISCLAIMER

Company fundamentals — revenue, gross profit, net income, shares outstanding, cash, total debt, and free cash flow — are drawn from SEC EDGAR and Financial Modeling Prep: SEC EDGAR XBRL company facts (data.sec.gov) for domestic filers, with a period-matched Financial Modeling Prep value where a filer is a foreign private issuer or discontinues a concept. Where a filer discontinues or freezes an XBRL concept (e.g. a gross-profit or long-term-debt tag), a period-matched Financial Modeling Prep value is substituted as a labeled fallback rather than carrying a stale figure.
ANALYST ESTIMATES & PRICE TARGETS
·
Forward revenue and EPS consensus — the FY-ahead estimate columns and the pro forma projections — are from Financial Modeling Prep analyst estimates: single-source, point-in-time, not guidance.
·
Per-firm price targets are from Financial Modeling Prep (price-target news and grades): the latest target per broker is kept, targets whose most recent call is over 18 months old are dropped, and statistical outliers (over 3× or under one-third of the panel median) are removed. VALUATION METHODOLOGIES
·

COMPANY & DESCRIPTIVE DATA

BASIS OF PRESENTATION

All monetary figures are presented in US dollars, in millions ($M), as filed. $B is used only on market-cap, enterprise-value and deal-value summary lines.
·
Period basis: the screening comparables (Public Company Screen) and the company-profile financial snapshot are computed on a last-twelve-months (LTM) basis — latest annual plus the most recent interim year-to-date, less the prior-year interim — the standard banker screening convention; the pro-forma and accretion model is built on latest-fiscal-year actuals plus forward analyst consensus (a normalized forward basis). This split is deliberate, not an inconsistency. Foreign private issuers without SEC interim (10-Q) filings, and any filer whose interim data does not tie out, are shown on a fiscal-year basis and labeled "FY".

Calendarization: where the two companies have different fiscal year-ends, the LTM screening basis is used specifically because it aligns their measurement windows to within approximately one month — materially reducing the fiscal-year-end offset that a same-labeled "FY" comparison would carry. APPENDIX I
Sources & Methodology
Data provenance and basis of presentation · Buyer: Alphabet Inc. · Target: Amazon Com Inc
PRICING & MARKET DATA
·
Live share prices and 52-week trading ranges for the Buyer and the Target are sourced from CNBC and Nasdaq (keyless, near-real-time), captured as of August 9, 2026 and cross-checked across feeds where two agree.
·
Equity value (market capitalization) shown as "current" reflects the live price multiplied by reported shares outstanding; where a live price is unavailable it is shown as "—" or "N/A".
·
Intraday quotes and 52-week extremes depend on feed availability; where no source returns a range, an illustrative range built from monthly closes is labeled as such.
COMPANY FUNDAMENTALS — PRIMARY FILINGS
·
Company fundamentals — revenue, gross profit, net income, shares outstanding, cash, total debt, and free cash flow — are drawn from SEC EDGAR and Financial Modeling Prep: SEC EDGAR XBRL company facts (data.sec.gov) for domestic filers, with a period-matched Financial Modeling Prep value where a filer is a foreign private issuer or discontinues a concept. All are period-matched to each company’s fiscal year. EPS is the reported diluted EPS; net income ÷ weighted-average diluted shares is a labeled fallback only where a filer does not report diluted EPS.
·
Figures reflect each company’s most recent annual report (Form 10-K for domestic filers, Form 20-F for foreign private issuers) and are used as-is, without restatement adjustments.
·
Where a filer discontinues or freezes an XBRL concept (e.g. a gross-profit or long-term-debt tag), a period-matched Financial Modeling Prep value is substituted as a labeled fallback rather than carrying a stale figure.
ANALYST ESTIMATES & PRICE TARGETS
·
Forward revenue and EPS consensus — the FY-ahead estimate columns and the pro forma projections — are from Financial Modeling Prep analyst estimates: single-source, point-in-time, not guidance.
·
Per-firm price targets are from Financial Modeling Prep (price-target news and grades): the latest target per broker is kept, targets whose most recent call is over 18 months old are dropped, and statistical outliers (over 3× or under one-third of the panel median) are removed. Buy / hold / sell reflects the latest grade per firm.
·
An independent consensus cross-check (mean / high / low) draws on Nasdaq and Financial Modeling Prep where available. Price targets are sell-side FORECASTS, not guarantees.
VALUATION METHODOLOGIES
·
The analyst price-target range and the 52-week trading range supply market reference points. Precedent-transaction multiples are omitted deck-wide — no sourceable comparable public-deal set is available on the current data stack.
COMPANY & DESCRIPTIVE DATA
·
Company descriptions, CEO, headquarters, employee counts, IPO date, sector / industry classification, beta, average trading volume, and company logos are from the Financial Modeling Prep company profile.
·
Segment, geography, and customer-mix figures, where shown, are illustrative and are not company-disclosed breakdowns.
·
The pro-forma forward columns use sell-side ANALYST CONSENSUS estimates (via Financial Modeling Prep) for forward revenue and EPS — these are analyst forecasts, not the app’s own model. The accretion, synergy and combination MATH applied on top of those inputs IS the app’s model. Multi-year synergy ramps are model assumptions, not guidance; forward operating expense is shown as "—" rather than estimated.
BASIS OF PRESENTATION
·
All monetary figures are presented in US dollars, in millions ($M), as filed. $B is used only on market-cap, enterprise-value and deal-value summary lines.
·
Period basis: the screening comparables (Public Company Screen) and the company-profile financial snapshot are computed on a last-twelve-months (LTM) basis — latest annual plus the most recent interim year-to-date, less the prior-year interim — the standard banker screening convention; the pro-forma and accretion model is built on latest-fiscal-year actuals plus forward analyst consensus (a normalized forward basis). This split is deliberate, not an inconsistency. Foreign private issuers without SEC interim (10-Q) filings, and any filer whose interim data does not tie out, are shown on a fiscal-year basis and labeled "FY".
·
Calendarization: where the two companies have different fiscal year-ends, the LTM screening basis is used specifically because it aligns their measurement windows to within approximately one month — materially reducing the fiscal-year-end offset that a same-labeled "FY" comparison would carry. Full calendar-year restatement is deliberately NOT applied: it would require estimating unfiled interim quarters (interpolation of periods no filer reports), and the residual period difference on the LTM basis is immaterial (under ~2% of the affected figures). The pro-forma / accretion model, being built on latest-fiscal-year actuals + forward consensus, pairs each company’s own latest fiscal year (relative years, not a common calendar period) — stated on that slide.
·
Enterprise value (EV) = equity value (market capitalization) + total debt − cash & marketable securities, taken from the same filing; figures for companies with active share-repurchase programs are approximate.
·
Profitability on the standalone P&L and comparative-profile slides — operating income, net income, diluted EPS, and operating/net margins — is shown on a Non-GAAP basis as reported in each company’s fiscal year-end earnings release (Form 8-K, Item 2.02), period-matched to the fiscal year shown and reconciled to GAAP; each line is labeled, and falls back to a GAAP-labeled figure where a reconciled non-GAAP value was unavailable. Gross profit, gross margin and operating expenses remain GAAP; EBITDA and its margins are computed (operating income + D&A); revenue and share counts are basis-neutral.
·
The accretion, pro forma and relative-contribution views are built on each company’s reported GAAP figures and are labeled accordingly.
·
Fiscal years follow each company’s own filing calendar: the Buyer FY2025, the Target FY2025.
·
Numbers are rounded for presentation; minor differences may arise from rounding.
TRANSACTION ASSUMPTIONS
·
Offer price, acquisition premium, and cash/stock consideration mix are user- or model-defined inputs.
·
Year 1–Year 3 synergies and transaction fees are user/model assumptions, not negotiated terms.
·
A 21% marginal tax rate and a 5% interest rate on acquisition debt are applied as standing model assumptions.
DISCLAIMER
·
This document is an educational illustration generated by EasyM&A to model a hypothetical combination of the Buyer and the Target.
·
It is NOT investment, financial, legal, or tax advice, NOT a recommendation or solicitation, and NOT an offer to buy or sell any security. It does not constitute a fairness opinion and MUST NOT be relied upon for any investment, purchase, sale, or other financial decision.
·
All outputs are hypothetical and must be independently verified against primary sources (SEC filings and live market data) before any decision. Market data as of August 9, 2026; subject to change.

BASIS OF PRESENTATION
